idiom_name: ASP.NET Core cookie authentication (AddCookie + SignInAsync) with Data Protection sealing the ticket
implementation_notes: The session state is the authentication ticket: AddCookie registers the handler, SignInAsync serializes the ClaimsPrincipal, encrypts and signs it with the Data Protection API and writes the cookie, and the middleware decrypts the cookie of the next request and populates HttpContext.User - nothing is stored server-side, so any instance can serve any request. That last property depends on the key ring: every instance in a farm must share Data Protection keys and the application discriminator, or cookies minted on one node fail to decrypt on another. Claims are a poor home for bulk session data (each claim is serialized into the client's cookie, and browsers cap a cookie near 4 KB), so keep the ticket small and push volume into a server-side store through ITicketStore; the hand-rolled form (serialize + MAC yourself) is only justified when a non-.NET issuer must accept the blob, and then a JWT should be used instead.
pitfalls: Data Protection keys are per machine by default: without a shared key ring and a fixed application name, users appear logged out at random as requests move between instances.
Everything put in claims ships in the cookie on every request, so secrets and large values belong in a server-side store behind ITicketStore, not in the ticket.
SignOutAsync only deletes the cookie: a stolen copy stays valid until the ticket expires, so keep ExpireTimeSpan short and treat key-ring rotation as the global kill switch.
SlidingExpiration rewrites the cookie on activity; with several tabs open the responses race and the last one can overwrite a newer ticket.
